text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the enticing Premier League clash between title contenders Arsenal and top-flight leaders Liverpool at Emirates Stadium.
Arsenal suffered from a December slump but have since responded with back-to-back Premier League victories over Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest.
The latter triumph at the City Ground, a 2-1 win on Tuesday, was far less convincing than the 5-0 thrashing of the Eagles.
However, Mikel Arteta’s men remain in the race for a top-flight title, trailing Liverpool by five points heading into this seismic clash.
Liverpool swept aside Chelsea with a 4-1 victory on Wednesday at Anfield, maintaining their lead at the Premier League summit despite pressure from Arsenal and Manchester City.

The Reds have still lost only once in the league all season, a 2-1 reverse at Tottenham back in September, with this another chance to consolidate their position in the title race and strike a blow to Arteta’s Gunners.
The headline team news for Arsenal is that Gabriel Jesus misses out through injury after scoring one and assisting another against Forest.
Havertz comes in to lead the line, while Smith Rowe drops to the bench for Jorginho in two Arteta changes to the hosts' lineup.
Klopp makes three changes from the midweek victory over Chelsea.
Conor Bradley misses out entirely after the death of his father, as does Dominik Szoboszlai, while injury doubt Nunez is on the bench.
Alexander-Arnold, Gravenberch and Gakpo are the trio to come in for Liverpool.
This will be the 200th league meeting between Arsenal and Liverpool, the fifth fixture to have been played as many times in English football history.
The Reds have won 79 to the Gunners' 66 so far (D54) – how important could a win for Arteta’s side be here?
Referee Anthony Taylor gets this huge Premier League clash under way!
Gakpo holds up a long Van Dijk pass before Jota, as he did against Chelsea, almost bundles through towards goal.
Raya is quick off his line, however, and intervenes before the Liverpool attacker can pounce.
The atmosphere inside the Emirates is matching the occasion so far, a hugely significant clash that will have a significant impact on the title race.
As for the moment, both sides continue to sound each other out.
Saka sneaks in behind after Odegaard squeezes past Van Dijk, only for the Arsenal winger to slice a right-footed cross out of play.
The Gunners are finding some joy down the right-hand side so far.
Arsenal players are incensed after referee Taylor points for a goal-kick, despite Alexander-Arnold twice seemingly conceding a corner on the far side.
The England right-back, perhaps, got away with one there.
Arsenal have opened the scoring in their last three Premier League games against Liverpool, doing so in the opening 10 minutes of the match each time.
They last scored first in four straight league meetings with the Reds between August 1967 and November 1970 (a run of six).
Can they repeat that feat here?
Diaz and Gomez look to burst down the left flank but the latter is denied by a wonderful sliding tackle by Rice.
The Arsenal midfielder covers so much ground, which is exactly why Arteta splashed the cash on the former West Ham man before the start of the season.
HUGE CHANCE! Gomez swings an inviting cross from the left-hand side but Raya claims before throwing for the onrushing Martinelli.
The Arsenal winger leaves Konate in his tracks, bursting into the area before his left-footed delivery is headed wide by Saka.
The England forward has to score from there but fails to make the required contact.
WIDE! Having seen Arsenal go close at one end, Liverpool respond down the other.
Mac Allister slots through for Gakpo, who breaks away from Saliba before dragging a right-footed strike just wide of the left-hand post.
GOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLLLLL! ARSENAL STRIKE FIRST! Lovely football from the Gunners at the back sees Zinchenko touch inside for Odegaard, who plays a first-time pass through for Havertz.
The Germany international is one-on-one with Alisson but fires straight at the Liverpool goalkeeper.
However, the rebound falls kindly to Saka, who takes a touch down before firing a left-footed effort into the unguarded net.
Arteta goes wild on the touchline and his side are 1-0 up!
Arsenal have won seven, drawn one and lost none when scoring the opening goal at home in the Premier League this season.
Can Arteta's side continue that run and strike a hammer blow to Liverpool's title hopes here?
Klopp will be frustrated so far, with Liverpool appearing somewhat shocked in the face of relentless Arsenal pressure.
The German head coach needs his experienced players, such as Van Dijk, to step up and calm proceedings down as the Emirates crowd continues to bounce in unison.
The Reds enjoy a spell of possession but do little with it.
Arsenal are sitting in a well-drilled formation, with two banks of four protecting Raya's goal.
For now, it remains 1-0 to the Gunners, who would move within two points of the league-leading Liverpool.
GREAT BLOCK! Alexander-Arnold makes a mess at the back as the Liverpool defender is hurried by Havertz.
A loose ball falls for Odegaard, who takes too much time on the edge of the area before Van Dijk blocks his left-footed drive.
Mac Allister loses possession in the middle but his error goes unpunished as Saka's aimless chip is collected by Gravenberch, who then wins a free-kick from Odegaard.
Mac Allister is dispossessed again by Rice before Havertz breaks over the halfway line.
Gomez needlessly tugs back on the Arsenal forward, conceding a free-kick before the referee cautions the Liverpool full-back.
Gomez could be in for a long game now, already on a caution and up against the impressive Saka.
Odegaard is leading the press for Arsenal, too, and dragging numerous Liverpool defenders all around as Klopp's men fail to figure how to cope at the Emirates so far.
Alexander-Arnold's right-wing cross has Gakpo interested before Gabriel prods back to Raya.
Arsenal are on top, make no mistake about it, but the Gunners must be wary of the Liverpool threat down either flank.
Gomez's searching diagonal finds Alexander-Arnold, whose cross is blocked behind by Zinchenko.
The Liverpool right-back delivers the right-sided corner towards the penalty spot but Van Dijk loops a poor header well over the target.
White makes the most of Mac Allister's nudge and wins a free-kick near the right-hand touchline.
The Arsenal right-back is deemed to take too long over restarting play, though, and is cautioned by referee Taylor.
There's a slight delay as referee Taylor drops something in the middle of the pitch before going over to fourth official Craig Pawson.
The pair discuss with one another as Pawson attempts to help Taylor with his equipment, seemingly changing his watch.
Bizarre!
Jorginho goes down and needs a moment to catch his breath after a foul from Gravenberch and Jota.
The former Chelsea midfielder is fine to continue, though, despite what looked like an uncomfortable collision.
Martinelli has more goal contributions against Liverpool in all competitions than he has against any other opponent for Arsenal (four goals, two assists).
The Brazilian netted the opener after just 58 seconds in this exact fixture last season, also assisting Saka’s goal to give the Gunners a 2-1 lead heading into half-time.
Alexander-Arnold has struggled to cope with him so far here, too.
SAVE! Odegaard and Rice work a short free-kick routine before the ball falls kindly for Gabriel.
The Arsenal centre-back has space on the edge of the area but his low left-footed curled attempt is held by Alisson, who gets down well to his right.
Liverpool have won their last four Premier League away games, scoring 10 goals and conceding just one.
It’s just one fewer win than they had in their previous 15 on the road in the league (W5 D7 L3).
However, the Reds look out of ideas in north London at the moment.
Gabriel angles a well-weighted pass for Martinelli but the Brazil winger is eased out the way by the industrious Konate.
Havertz is then deemed to have fouled Mac Allister near the halfway line, perhaps fortunate to escape a caution for his sliding tackle.
Diaz catches the ankle of White with a late challenge, with the Arsenal right-back making the most of the foul.
Referee Taylor is quick to blow his whistle, but no further punishment follows for the Colombia winger.
An entertaining first half is almost coming to an end as fourth official Pawson indicates a minimum of three additional minutes.
Klopp's half-time message will be an interesting one at this rate.
Jorginho slides a deft pass into the feet of Martinelli, who fails to pull the trigger inside the Liverpool area.
The Arsenal winger just could not sort his feet out to test Alisson.
GOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLLL! LIVERPOOL EQUALISE! It is agony for Arsenal on the stroke of half-time as the visitors level to make it 1-1.
Gravenberch clips an inviting pass over the top for Diaz, though Saliba gets there first and looks to shield back for Raya.
The Liverpool winger manages to poke in front of the defensive pair, with his prod deflecting off Gabriel and slipping over the line.
It goes down as a Gabriel own goal and the Premier League leaders are back in this contest!
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 1-1 LIVERPOOL
Arteta's men appear dejected as the half-time whistle sounds with Arsenal and Liverpool level at 1-1 heading into the break.
Saka fired the hosts into the lead after 14 minutes, capitalising on a rebound from Havertz's shot that was saved by Alisson.

The Gunners remained in control for the rest of the first half, only for Saliba and Raya to make a mess on the stroke of half-time as Diaz poked against Gabriel, whose own goal dragged the Reds back into this contest.
Amazingly, Liverpool are level in this Premier League clash despite not having a shot on target yet.
Arsenal have accumulated 1.94 expected goals (xG) to the Reds' 0.1, yet somehow these two sides cannot be separated at the interval.
Arteta needs his side to find a clinical edge in the next period, while Klopp's men must still respond after a woeful first-half performance that was only salvaged by Arsenal's defensive error.
Arteta wastes no time at the break, bringing off Zinchenko for Kiwior.
It remains unclear whether that decision was injury-enforced or tactical.
Referee Taylor gets the second half under way in north London!
CLOSE! Diaz almost makes an immediate impact in the next half, driving down the left before his right-footed effort is blocked by White.
Liverpool regain possession in the middle before Mac Allister rockets a long-range strike just wide to Raya's right when aiming for the top corner.
It looks like a tactical tweak from Klopp as Jones sits a little deeper alongside Mac Allister.
The former sends a long pass down the left flank for Diaz, who has acres of space but his cross fails to find attacking team-mate Jota in the middle.
WIDE! It is one-way traffic to start the second half.
Diaz wanders forward before offloading to Jones, who cuts inside from the left of the area before whipping a right-footed attempt wide of Raya's left-hand post.
This is so much better from Klopp's visitors.
Odegaard touches a smart first-time pass through for Havertz but the makeshift Arsenal forward is bumped out the way by Konate.
The Liverpool centre-back continues to dominate in one-on-one defensive situations.
SO CLOSE! Alexander-Arnold is caught napping at the back as Jorginho passes through for Havertz, who tees up Odegaard.
The Norway midfielder dances onto his left foot before his rasping drive is deflected just wide of Alisson's right-hand post by Konate.
Jota has tons of time from Alexander-Arnold's pass but his left-wing cross is comfortably headed away by Saliba.
It appears Klopp is readying some changes on the touchline as Odegaard fells Jones in the middle.
Saka hooks a clearance long and Konate scrambles under pressure.
The Liverpool centre-back cannot get around Havertz, dragging the Arsenal forward down and going into referee Taylor's book for a cynical foul.
CHANCE! Odegaard hovers over a deep central free-kick before chipping a left-footed cross towards the far post.
Gabriel makes the first contact but can only slide a poor header wide to Alisson's left.
Gabriel is the next Arsenal man to be shown a yellow card after pushing an arm into the face of Gakpo, who was spinning to race onto Alexander-Arnold's throughball.
Klopp makes a double change.
Alexander-Arnold comes off from right-back, with Robertson coming on.
The Scotland international will slot in on the left, with Gomez moving over to the other flank.
Gakpo, after that foul from Gabriel, also makes way for Nunez, who was only deemed fit enough for the bench in this clash.
In fact, it is a triple change! Klopp also sends on Elliott for Gravenberch, whose pass for Diaz created the uncertainty for Liverpool to equalise on the stroke of half-time.
Gomez is soon involved in his new right-back position, winning a corner for his side.
Robertson whips the set-piece toward the near post but Havertz intervenes at the near post to head clear.
Saka is down inside the Arsenal area, holding his neck after some apparent discomfort following what appeared to be an arm from team-mate Gabriel.
The England winger will be fine to continue, even if slightly confused to be caught by his colleague in defence.
OPENING! Rice bursts forward, powering past Diaz on halfway before offloading to his right.
Saka runs at Robertson, cutting inside from the flank before curling a left-footed effort well over Alisson's target, albeit via a deflection.
Rice's inswinging corner heads towards a congested near-post area but the result is a Liverpool goal-kick.
Alisson continues to be crowded from any set-piece chance but, for now, remains untested.
ARSENAL WANT A PENALTY! Martinelli receives possession on the left-hand touchline and sends a throughball down the flank for Havertz.
The Arsenal makeshift forward gets in front of Mac Allister but is dispossessed by his recovering tackle.
The Gunners appeal for a penalty but referee Taylor shakes his head.
The VAR then sticks with the on-field call.
Across his five appearances at the Emirates for Liverpool, Jota has averaged a goal or assist every 41 minutes in all competitions before this game (five goals, two assists in 287 minutes).

Indeed, since the start of 2020-21 (his first season with the Reds), Mohamed Salah (seven at Old Trafford) is the only Premier League player to have scored more goals at an away ground in all competitions than Jota’s five at Arsenal.
He has yet to get involved here, though.
GOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLL! ARSENAL LEAD AGAIN! Van Dijk and Alisson, what are you doing? Gabriel launches a long, somewhat aimless, pass over the Liverpool defence.
Van Dijk hovers but does not intervene, with Alisson coming out and missing his clearance entirely.
Martinelli, perhaps not believing his luck, accepts an unthinkable gift to roll a right-footed strike into a completely open goal.
Arteta’s side are 2-1 up in bizarre circumstances!
Martinelli has more goal contributions against Liverpool in all competitions than he has against any other opponent for Arsenal (five goals, two assists).
The Brazil winger will never be granted a simpler finish against the Reds than that one, though.
Mac Allister looks to respond for Liverpool, driving forward before pulling a left-footed strike wide to Raya's left.
The Emirates is rocking as Arsenal fans start to dream of a title charge.
Kiwior is cautioned after an earlier foul on Jota, with referee Taylor coming back to punish the Arsenal defender when play pauses.
Arsenal have taken five points from their last three Premier League games against Liverpool (W1 D2), as many as they had in their previous 12 (W1 D2 L9).
They’re looking to remain unbeaten in four league games against the Reds for the first time since between December 2014 and January 2016 (W1 D3).
That could be on the cards here.
Robertson advances down the inside left-hand channel but Saka is aware, moving to his right before clearing Jones' throughball.
Arsenal will continue to sit deep now, defending their lead as the final stages approach.
Arteta opts for fresh legs up top.
Martinelli, whose goal proves the difference at the moment, trudges off to be replaced by Trossard.
Elliott lifts a right-wing delivery towards the back post, where Raya claims before the Arsenal goalkeeper rolls out for Rice.
His long pass for Trossard is then poor, however, and Liverpool settle for a throw-in.
CLOSE! Kiwior is forced into more defensive action, tackling behind for a corner against Gomez.
Robertson wanders over to take the set-piece, swinging a near-post cross that is headed away by Havertz.
Mac Allister waits on the edge of the area, hammering a volley just wide to Raya's left.
So close for the visitors.
Saka requires medical attention from the Arsenal physios, seemingly struggling from an issue with his right leg.
Arteta watches on, perhaps anxiously, as the England international holds his head.
Could this be the end of his game?
Saka is unable to continue, limping off with a right-leg injury.
The Arsenal winger makes way for Nelson, who goes straight over to the right-hand side against Robertson.
Nelson skips around Konate but is then confused as referee Taylor has pulled play back for a foul throw.
That decision does not go down too well with the home crowd, nor Arteta on the touchline.
Liverpool have scored in each of their last 17 Premier League games against Arsenal since a goalless draw in August 2015.
Overall, they’re the only side to score 100+ goals against the Gunners in the competition (109).
The Reds need a late equaliser here.
Gomez and Kiwior go head-to-head once again as the Arsenal left-back defends behind for a corner.
Robertson will come over to take this one...
Robertson's right-sided corner is cleared by the head of Gabriel.
Trossard thinks about a counter-attacking break before opting to go backwards.
Jorginho then has a similar though but once again prefers the cautious option in possession.
CHANCES! Arsenal remain patient in possession before Odegaard cuts inside from the right-hand flank.
The Arsenal midfielder curls towards the unmarked Kiwior, who heads straight at Alisson.
Down the other end, Nunez races onto a long pass in behind before hammering a wild right-footed strike well over the target.
Klopp enters last-chance saloon in this game, sending on midfielder Thiago for Gomez.
The Spain international returns to action for the first time since April.
Martinelli has scored five goals against Liverpool, his joint-most versus a single side for Arsenal (level with Crystal Palace).
In addition, no player has been directly involved in more league goals against the Reds since the start of last term (three goals, two assists).
His second-half strike is the difference at the moment.
LIVERPOOL ARE DOWN TO 10! Elliott's cross is headed away by the Arsenal defence before Nelson looks to counter-attack.
The substitute winger dances past Konate in the middle, leaving referee Taylor with no choice.
The Liverpool centre-back receives his second yellow card and the Reds go a man down!
The home crowd are bewildered after Van Dijk clatters into Havertz in an aerial duel.
Referee Taylor points for a Liverpool free-kick, infuriating the Arsenal supporters and Jorginho.
The VAR checks the tackle for potential dangerous play by Van Dijk, but the original decision stands.
Nunez is cautioned for his furious reaction after the referee does not give a free-kick when Gabriel pulls him back near the halfway line.
Tempers are boiling over in north London!
Frustrated by how long Saliba takes over a deep free-kick, the Arsenal centre-back is shown a yellow card by referee Taylor.
It has not been the most disciplined Premier League clash, let's put it that way.
The Arsenal crowd, amid the chaos of Nunez and Saliba cautions, were far from impressed as the fourth official indicates seven additional minutes.
However, that will not matter as the Gunners are in once again...
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLL! 3-1 ARSENAL! Look away, again, Alisson.
The Liverpool goalkeeper can only hold his hands up once more, having already made a mistake for Martinelli’s strike earlier in the half.
Trossard is played in by Kiwior’s pass, dancing past Elliott and Diaz before driving a left-footed strike towards the near post.
Alisson should save the low effort but it goes through his legs as the Brazil international disappoints for a second time at the Emirates.
Kiwior takes the credit for the assist, with his simple pass finding Trossard, who does the rest with a slice of fortune after his finish squirms past Alisson.
Klopp cuts a frustrated figure on the touchline.
Having already made a mistake against Martinelli, Alisson fails to make a simple save against Trossard.
Arteta's side are going to cut the gap to two points at the Premier League summit.
There could be more post-match punishment for these two sides.
It is more ill-discipline as Rice hacks down Diaz in the middle, with the Arsenal midfielder shown a yellow card for his cynical tackle.
Another one! Havertz exchanges a few words with the assistant referee after a throw-in decision in the far corner.
Taylor will not stand for the dissent and cautions the makeshift Arsenal forward.
Renewed belief engulfs the Emirates as the full-time whistle approaches.
Liverpool are heading towards just their second league loss of the season, with this defeat a cruel blow in their title hopes.
This is not what Klopp will have envisaged at all.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 3-1 LIVERPOOL
Suddenly, Arsenal throw the Premier League title race wide open after a 3-1 victory over the league-leading Liverpool at Emirates Stadium.
Saka opened the scoring after 14 minutes, prodding in a routine rebound after Havertz was denied from close range.
A needless Saliba mistake allowed the Reds a way back into the contest on the stroke of half-time, with Diaz sneaking in to prod a low cross off Gabriel for an own goal.
Klopp’s tactical tweaks seemed to have the visitors back in the game in the second half, only for Van Dijk and Alisson to comically fail to communicate and tee up the simplest of Martinelli goals.
It did not improve for the Liverpool goalkeeper either as Trossard rolled a tame finish through his legs to seal victory in the 92nd minute.
Arteta’s men move within two points of Liverpool at the top-flight summit, ahead of the Gunners’ visit to West Ham on Sunday.
The Reds must find a response when they host relegation-threatened Burnley on Saturday.
That is all for now, until next time.
Goodbye for now!
